scope: Repository-wide comparative research with F02/F03/F05 and scoped F16/F04/F11 implementation updates on 2026-10-16. Original research scores, ranks and proposed future work retained. F01 remains on hold. Current verification is in the two implementation records.
popularity_method: Reach bands: <=10 stars=1; <=100=2; <=1000=3; <=5000=5; <=10000=7; <=25000=8; <=100000=9; above=10. PowerToys Awake reach capped at 6 because stars cover the suite. P=round(0.6*max donor reach+0.4*min(10,2*donor count)); no matched donor P=1. This is an ecosystem visibility proxy, not measured feature demand.
priority_method: round(0.55*usefulness+0.20*fit+0.15*popularity+0.10*(11-effort),1). Rank current candidates descending, then usefulness, then ID; deferred-by-user items have null rank. Original research_rank is retained. Risk/dependencies/qualification override score.
effort_method: 1-10 relative complexity. 1-3: 2-4 engineer days; 4-6: 5-10; 7-8: 11-20; 9-10: 21-40. Rough initial engineering estimates include local fixtures, exclude physical qualification, signing procurement, translation and community acceptance.

sources.name: Twinkle Tray
sources.evidence: Brightness flyout, hotkeys, normalization, time/idle changes, contrast, CLI, localization and package managers.

sources.name: Monitorian
sources.evidence: Individual/unison brightness, adjustable ranges, renaming, capability probe/rescan, languages and SDR content brightness history. Paid add-on code is excluded.

sources.name: Lively Wallpaper
sources.evidence: Local video and other presentations, Windows screensaver integration, CLI, background-app and coverage pause algorithms, translations.

sources.name: PowerToys Awake
sources.evidence: Timed/expiring keep-awake, separate screen-on option, PID/parent lifetime and CLI. Reach capped because suite stars do not measure Awake adoption.

sources.name: Auto Dark Mode
sources.evidence: Solar/sensor switching, delayed changes, battery behavior, accent switching, updates, translations and package managers.

sources.name: LittleBigMouse
sources.evidence: Display layout adjustments, mixed-DPI pointer routing, border resistance, live changes and display diagnostics.

sources.name: ScreenBlind
sources.evidence: Selective password overlays, cursor trapping and additional native scene styles. These are product claims, not Windows secure desktop guarantees.

features.title: Full command interface and local IPC
features.value: Makes DAC usable from shortcuts, scripts and external controllers without editing live settings.
features.gap: The public CLI can launch, stop, report version/help and select a config directory; it cannot list displays, query state, start/stop one presentation, choose a profile or snooze.
implementation: Define versioned request/reply structs and typed actions shared by tray and CLI. Add list, status, start, dismiss, snooze and profile actions; distinguish dismiss from existing --stop shutdown.

Use bounded local IPC with an explicit logon-SID ACL, remote-client rejection and user/session validation. Dispatch immutable requests to the UI owner; return snapshots with exit codes and a JSON output option.
Resolve stable IDs against a catalog generation. Keep the singleton scoped per user/session, reject unknown targets and require a separate hardware action that cannot grant permission.
acceptance: Concurrent clients cannot create a second controller or race topology changes into a different target.
Malformed/oversized requests, cross-session access, disconnected targets and busy/shutting-down owners fail predictably.
Existing --stop semantics, emergency recovery and independent-peer idle histories remain intact.

features.title: Compact per-display control flyout
features.value: Reduces the number of interactions needed to understand and control several monitors.
features.gap: Visible accessibility, mixed-DPI, real session/topology and physical display qualification remain outstanding; see docs/FEATURE_IMPLEMENTATION.md.
implementation: Build a native keyboard-accessible flyout showing one row per connected target: name, presentation, inhibition reason, next deadline and start/dismiss controls.
Read the existing explanation snapshot on the UI thread; reuse current commands and permission checks rather than creating another controller.
Keep a stable selection across topology updates and expose equivalent text to accessibility tools.
acceptance: Each action affects the chosen stable target while peers retain state.
Rows remain usable at 100-200% DPI, high contrast and with keyboard/screen reader navigation.
No shell, media or DDC work runs synchronously while opening or refreshing the flyout.
features.research_gap: Tray menus and selected-monitor explanations exist; there is no compact all-display surface with simultaneous status, reason, countdown and direct actions.
features.verification: Release and Debug each passed 28/28 isolated CTests; production static analysis and PE checks passed. Visible/physical qualification remains outstanding; see implementation record.

features.title: Persistent friendly display names
features.value: Makes similar monitors recognizable in settings, tray actions and scripts.
features.gap: Visible accessibility, mixed-DPI, real session/topology and physical display qualification remain outstanding; see docs/FEATURE_IMPLEMENTATION.md.
implementation: Persist a bounded UTF-8 display nickname keyed by stable identity in a versioned schema; preserve disconnected names.
Use the nickname only for display text. Keep IDs authoritative and permit duplicate names without ambiguous command resolution.
Redact nicknames in diagnostics because a name may contain personal information.
acceptance: Names survive reorder, reconnect and settings roundtrip without transferring hardware authority.
Empty, duplicate and non-Latin names render safely; invalid lengths/encoding are rejected.
Diagnostics still contain only approved Display N aliases.
features.research_gap: OS labels and temporary Display N overlays exist, but users cannot save their own names.
features.verification: Release and Debug each passed 28/28 isolated CTests; production static analysis and PE checks passed. Visible/physical qualification remains outstanding; see implementation record.

features.title: Per-display temporary keep-awake leases
features.value: Lets one screen stay available for a meeting while unused peers continue protecting themselves.
features.gap: Visible accessibility, mixed-DPI, real session/topology and physical display qualification remain outstanding; see docs/FEATURE_IMPLEMENTATION.md.
implementation: Add runtime leases with stable target sets, monotonic deadlines and explicit cancel controls; keep them separate from persisted monitor enablement.
Treat an absolute local expiry as an input resolved to a deadline with stated clock-change behavior. On expiry establish fresh idle boundaries only for affected nodes.
Show active leases in explanations and the flyout; session exit clears them. This inhibits DAC activation and does not by itself inhibit Windows sleep.
acceptance: A lease for A neither wakes nor resets B, including under shared/media policies.
Expiry, cancellation, suspend/resume and clock changes follow documented rules.
Imported configurations cannot silently create runtime leases.
features.research_gap: Current snooze is global with fixed tray durations. Per-target leases, custom durations and an absolute expiry are missing.
features.verification: Release and Debug each passed 28/28 isolated CTests; production static analysis and PE checks passed. Visible/physical qualification remains outstanding; see implementation record.

features.title: Display capability inspector and rescan report
features.value: Explains why a target is ineligible or quarantined and prepares hardware expansion without guesswork.
features.gap: Read-only cached inspector, explicit OS-only rescan and redacted report implemented. New physical DDC/capability probing remains deferred; no supported compatibility claim. Visible/physical qualification pending.
implementation: Cached read-only inspector with OS identity/connection/geometry/eligibility, policy/deadlines, separate saved hardware permission and observed state, fault/recovery freshness.
Coalesced asynchronous OS-only rescan; epoch rejection, unchanged-topology preservation, failed/partial-read stale retention and redacted summary.
New live physical DDC probing and capability-string reads remain deferred; no compatibility support inferred from saved grants or synthetic tests.
acceptance: Opening diagnostics never sends DDC commands.
Canceled, hung and malformed capability responses are bounded and shown as unknown rather than supported.
Reconnect invalidates the right cache; clone targets and quarantine cannot become eligible through rescan.
features.research_gap: Catalog refresh, faults and redacted diagnostics exist; there is no structured user-facing capability/probe view.
features.verification: Final Release 29/29 (102.54 s), Debug 29/29 (109.21 s), 117665 policy assertions each; zero production analyzer findings; both PE checks and diff check passed. Private/hidden fixtures only; see docs/INSPECTOR_MAP_BACKGROUND.md and evidence/inspector-map-background-20261016/verification.json.
research_implementation: First expose cached topology, identity eligibility, fault state and observation age without issuing hardware queries.
Add a separate explicit capability probe on the contained worker/helper path; cache by device/connection epoch and preserve unknown/timeout states.
Offer a redacted summary by default and an explicit identifiable local export for support. Read queries can still stall a driver.

features.title: Visual display map for target selection
features.value: Helps users choose the correct physical screen before changing a presentation or policy.
features.gap: Native desktop-pixel spatial map, stable selection, parallel native keyboard list and guarded controls/settings/inspector navigation implemented. Visible accessibility and actual mixed-DPI/topology qualification pending.
implementation: Native aspect-preserving desktop-pixel rectangles and parallel keyboard list, stable-ID selection, textual legend/status, guarded settings/controls/inspector navigation.
Theme/high-contrast, DPI and focus retention implemented; real visible/topology qualification remains separate.
acceptance: Fixtures cover mixed DPI, portrait layouts, negative coordinates and clone targets.
Selection remains attached to identity across reordering; stale map actions are rejected.
Visible acceptance confirms that labels and keyboard focus match physical displays.
features.research_gap: DAC provides a dropdown and identify overlays, but no spatial map of the current desktop.
features.verification: Final Release 29/29 (102.54 s), Debug 29/29 (109.21 s), 117665 policy assertions each; zero production analyzer findings; both PE checks and diff check passed. Private/hidden fixtures only; see docs/INSPECTOR_MAP_BACKGROUND.md and evidence/inspector-map-background-20261016/verification.json.
research_implementation: Render scaled rectangles from the catalog with names, enabled state and a selected target; provide a parallel accessible list.
Use signed coordinates and preserve aspect ratios across rotated and negative-coordinate outputs. Mark clone/unknown targets as ineligible.
Keep this map read-only with respect to Windows layout; opening it must not activate presentations.

features.title: Rules for background running applications
features.value: Supports long tasks or applications that should inhibit protection even after losing focus.
features.gap: Persistent schema5 running-application rules, explicit stable/global scopes, bounded user/session process worker, limited uncertain grace and native draft settings implemented. Real session/application qualification pending.
implementation: Schema5 persistent enabled full-path or explicit filename rules with stable-target/global scope; native draft editor and profile transfers.
One-Hz bounded current-user/session executable observation, live owned-job exclusion, epoch rejection, per-rule Present/Absent/Unknown and at most five seconds prior-positive grace.
Targeted boundaries preserve independent peers/inhibitors; imports disarm automation/hardware and diagnostics omit application identities.
acceptance: Foreground-only rules keep existing semantics; process rules cannot accidentally become global.
Stale/denied process observations, exited tasks and owned saver processes behave predictably.
Measure scan overhead with many processes and confirm no UI/input-path blocking.
features.research_gap: Rules currently match foreground apps or ignore audio; they do not match a bounded snapshot of background processes.
features.verification: Final Release 29/29 (102.54 s), Debug 29/29 (109.21 s), 117665 policy assertions each; zero production analyzer findings; both PE checks and diff check passed. Private/hidden fixtures only; see docs/INSPECTOR_MAP_BACKGROUND.md and evidence/inspector-map-background-20261016/verification.json.
research_implementation: Add a distinct running-process rule kind; scan on a worker at a bounded interval and match full paths by default.
Require explicit global or selected-monitor scope because a background process has no reliable foreground display.
Publish timestamped observations with a stale-state policy and explain which rule blocks a target without logging paths by default.

features.title: Process-bound temporary keep-awake leases
features.value: Keeps selected displays available while a specific task runs and removes the exception automatically when it ends.
features.gap: Foreground executable rules exist; there is no explicit temporary lease attached to one live process instance.
implementation: Bind a lease to a retained process handle and creation identity, with a maximum timeout and an explicit target set.
Observe process exit away from the input path, then enqueue lease removal on the UI thread. A reused PID must never inherit the lease.
Use a native process picker for the current roadmap; expose access-denied and exited-process outcomes without widening scope. A CLI option can be reconsidered only if F01 is restored.
acceptance: Process exit, crash, PID reuse and denied handle access cannot leave an indefinite inhibitor.
Only selected monitors receive a new idle boundary on lease removal.
Owned DAC saver/helper processes cannot create recursive self-inhibition.

features.title: Weekday schedules and date exceptions
features.value: Allows different weekday/weekend routines without editing daily profiles.
features.gap: Profiles support daily HH:MM windows, including overnight periods, but no weekdays or explicit date exclusions. This is a DAC-specific extension, not an observed donor feature.
implementation: Introduce a weekday mask and bounded local-date exception list with a schema migration preserving existing every-day behavior.
Define an overnight interval as owned by its starting day. Keep manual > foreground-app > scheduled > base precedence and show why a profile won.
Use an injected civil clock to reevaluate DST, timezone changes and resume; avoid replaying missed activations.
acceptance: Test Friday-to-Saturday overnight, exclusive ends, DST gaps/repeats and overlapping profiles.
Old settings retain their meaning; import continues to disarm automatic and hardware authority.
The schedule editor previews the next matching interval and reports conflicts deterministically.

features.title: Localization infrastructure and translated UI
features.value: Makes setup and recovery understandable to a broader audience.
features.gap: UI strings are predominantly inline English and the resources declare an English version-information language.
implementation: Extract strings into stable resource IDs, keep persisted enums/keys language-neutral and retain English fallback.
Start with one pilot locale and longer-string pseudo-localization; use locale-aware date/time formatting and inspect native layout sizing.
Keep diagnostics machine fields stable and resource updates separately reviewable; plan RTL support explicitly rather than assuming it.
acceptance: Missing translations fall back without losing emergency/recovery text.
Long strings, Unicode, keyboard accelerators and 100-200% DPI do not clip controls.
Configuration roundtrips unchanged across language selection and translated UI remains accessible.

features.title: Actual monitor brightness control
features.value: Adds true brightness reduction before covering a monitor and manual adjustment from DAC.
features.gap: Dim is software overlay opacity; current DDC support implements power off/wake only, not brightness.
implementation: Introduce a separate brightness grant and capability model, independent of the current hardware-power flag. Use DDC for eligible external monitors and investigate WMI for built-in panels.
Extend a separately contained helper protocol with typed brightness operations, rate limits, cancellation and bounded target identity validation.
Record prior value and the last applied value. Restore only if DAC still owns that value, so another controller or the user is not overwritten.
acceptance: Simulation covers timeout, wrong target, permission revocation, concurrent controllers and restoration conflicts.
Physical checks cover exact monitor/adapter combinations with recovery available.
Never describe overlay dimming as hardware brightness or infer energy savings from a percentage.

features.title: Battery and AC profile triggers
features.value: Changes complete protection policies when a laptop moves between power sources.
features.gap: The existing batteryBlack flag changes expensive content to black; it cannot select a full battery-specific profile.
implementation: Add an explicit AC/DC trigger to profiles and document where it sits relative to app and scheduled matches.
Reuse the existing power-source adapter and debounce; Unknown must preserve a conservative, explainable policy.
Continue applying base hardware grants and enablement caps after profile selection.
acceptance: Rapid source changes and Unknown readings do not thrash ownership or enable DDC.
Manual profiles retain precedence and old batteryBlack behavior remains available.
Injected AC/DC transitions and visible laptop resume tests agree.

features.title: Package manager distribution
features.value: Makes finding, installing and updating qualified releases easier.
features.gap: DAC has a verified local portable ZIP workflow, but no maintained public package-manager manifest.
implementation: After a qualified signed release exists, prepare a versioned WinGet or Scoop manifest tied to immutable artifact hashes.
Define portable extraction, user data retention, startup path handling and update/uninstall behavior before publishing.
Validate manifests locally; package-manager submission and release publication remain separate delivery actions.
acceptance: Clean-machine install/update/remove preserve preferences and never enable startup or DDC implicitly.
Every manifest references the expected architecture, version and verified artifact hash.
Moving the executable cannot leave an unnoticed stale login entry.

features.title: Coverage-aware application inhibition
features.value: Reduces false activation when several visible windows collectively cover a monitor.
features.gap: Foreground/fullscreen overlap exists; DAC does not calculate collective visible coverage as an optional inhibitor.
implementation: Prototype bounded window coverage on a worker with a configurable threshold and hysteresis; start with opaque ordinary windows.
Exclude DAC-owned covers and previews, hidden/cloaked/minimized windows and irrelevant desktops. Keep the current simple policy as default.
Present the result as a heuristic; uncertainty must not invent precise media or tab attribution.
acceptance: Fixtures cover tiled windows, overlays, transparent windows, moving windows and multiple outputs.
A covered A does not inhibit B; DAC's own cover cannot sustain its own inhibitor.
Visible gaming tests check exclusive/fullscreen behavior and CPU cost before enabling by default.

features.title: Keep Windows awake while DAC manages displays
features.value: Supports downloads or compute jobs while DAC continues using black or other presentations on idle screens.
features.gap: DAC observes display requests but does not create a user-requested system keep-awake lifetime.
implementation: Add a separate opt-in system-power lease using a Windows power request with a visible reason and clear/close ownership on every exit path.
Default to a system-only request. Any screen-on request is global Windows behavior and must be labeled separately from DAC per-display inhibition.
Respect explicit sleep/session policy and document Modern Standby and DC limitations; do not modify persistent power plans.
acceptance: Injected API failures and every cancellation path release request ownership.
Windows sleep, lock and battery behavior are checked in an isolated visible session.
The UI never implies that Windows display requests provide per-monitor power authority.

features.title: Scheduled and idle hardware brightness stages
features.value: Can reduce brightness gradually before native black or select different brightness targets by time.
features.gap: DAC has dim/fade and timed black/power stages; those stages do not drive hardware brightness.
implementation: Model brightness as a separately owned stage with explicit entry, cancellation and restoration rules. Coalesce intermediate values to limit DDC traffic.
Reuse profile scheduling and never let schedules grant hardware authority.
Resolve manual brightness, time profile and idle-stage precedence explicitly; topology/session transitions invalidate pending writes.
acceptance: Input during a ramp cancels stale operations and restores only owned values.
Schedule overlap, wake and helper timeout do not repeat writes indefinitely.
Physical acceptance measures actual responsiveness separately from synthetic timing.

features.title: Explicit Windows workstation lock action
features.value: Offers an unambiguous security action for users who might otherwise confuse black presentations with locking.
features.gap: DAC deliberately does not lock Windows. ScreenBlind's password overlay motivates this adaptation, but is not evidence of secure workstation locking.
implementation: Add a clearly named explicit Lock Windows command using the OS lock API; the first version should be manual only.
Retire/hide owned presentations and let existing session notifications handle lock/unlock. Check the asynchronous result through session state.
Defer automatic locking until whole-session idle semantics are specified; never lock solely because one secondary display is idle.
acceptance: An API fixture verifies request handling without locking the operator's session.
Visible tests in an isolated session confirm lock/unlock and cover cleanup.
No DAC password database, cursor trapping or claim of per-monitor OS locking is introduced.

features.title: Brightness calibration and synchronized groups
features.value: Makes one user-facing brightness adjustment behave more consistently across unlike panels.
features.gap: DAC has no hardware brightness ranges, calibration curves or linked adjustment groups.
implementation: Store per-target user min/max and a monotonic normalized mapping; retain native values for diagnostics only with user choice.
Apply a group intent as independent bounded requests. Report partial success without claiming an atomic physical update.
Let users adjust perceived equality; avoid presenting percentage matching as measured luminance calibration.
acceptance: Mappings are monotonic and clamped; invalid ranges cannot send out-of-range values.
A disconnected or failed group member does not redirect changes to another display.
Restoration ownership and explicit grants remain per device.

features.title: Opt-in update notifications
features.value: Helps users notice fixes once qualified releases exist.
features.gap: DAC is offline and has no updater; this is a deliberate change to its product contract.
implementation: Prefer package-manager updates first. If demand remains, add manual or opt-in metadata checks in a worker with a timeout and no device/configuration upload.
Show a release link and verified version information; avoid self-replacement while presentations or helpers are active.
Keep offline launches fast and default behavior unchanged. A full automatic updater requires a separate rollback/signature design.
acceptance: Offline, malformed metadata, proxy failure and version rollback responses cannot block startup.
Disabled checking produces no network requests.
A notification cannot execute downloaded code or mutate hardware/startup permissions.

features.title: Sunrise and sunset profile triggers
features.value: Can align presentation and timeout preferences with daylight without daily manual adjustment.
features.gap: DAC has fixed local times only; it has no solar calculation or location setting.
implementation: Use a deterministic local solar calculation with manually supplied approximate coordinates and offsets; avoid a mandatory location/network service.
Represent polar-day/no-event outcomes explicitly, use timezone-aware civil dates and offer a fixed-time fallback.
Do not add geolocation to exported diagnostics. Keep solar triggers below manual/application precedence.
acceptance: Reference vectors cover hemispheres, DST and polar cases.
Missing coordinates or an unavailable event produces a visible fallback instead of an arbitrary activation.
Offline operation and configuration disarming remain intact.

features.title: Additional configurable native scenes
features.value: Adds variety at lower runtime cost than embedding a browser or video engine.
features.gap: DAC already has moving clock, constellation, themes and rotation; new scene types and per-scene density/speed/clock format are missing.
implementation: Add one low-luminance native scene and bounded speed/density/clock-format options rather than an executable plugin system.
Reuse draft preview, scene deadlines, palettes and battery fallback. Keep motion independent of media/input attribution.
Validate each parameter and use a deterministic test clock/random seed for rendering fixtures.
acceptance: Worst-case settings stay within measured paint/resource budgets.
Input dismisses the new scene through the existing path; low-power and black transitions still work.
Visible acceptance checks high contrast settings UI, mixed DPI and repeated static elements.

features.title: Runtime accent selection
features.value: Lets users personalize the settings UI without rebuilding DAC.
features.gap: System/light/dark and high contrast exist; seven Fujin accent presets are build-time choices only.
implementation: Generate an allowlisted table of all pinned Fujin palettes at build time and choose an index in host preferences.
Refresh existing controls in place while preserving drafts/focus. High contrast must continue to override custom palettes.
Do not change low-luminance scene colors when a settings accent changes.
acceptance: Each generated palette passes integrity validation and contrast review.
Old host preferences migrate to the current default; unknown accent values fail safely.
Changing accents retains drafts, focus and high-contrast behavior.

features.title: HDR awareness and SDR content brightness investigation
features.value: Makes display state clearer and could improve appearance consistency on HDR desktops.
features.gap: Physical HDR appearance is unqualified, and DAC has no HDR capability status or SDR content brightness setting.
implementation: Start with read-only HDR state and visible qualification of black/scenes/slides; keep that deliverable independent of a brightness setter.
Investigate a supported SDR brightness setter for the pinned SDK/OS baseline. Monitorian's product history establishes the feature, not API suitability for DAC.
If only undocumented operations are available, retain read-only status and defer writing. Keep hardware brightness, SDR content brightness and overlay opacity distinct.
acceptance: HDR state changes invalidate cached presentation assumptions safely.
A prototype must establish API support, restoration and exact-target behavior before any setter is scheduled.
Document visible black-level/clock results on representative HDR and SDR displays.

features.title: Local video and animated media presentations
features.value: Adds visual variety for users who prefer moving content to black or the existing scenes.
features.gap: Photo extensions include GIF, but SlideFrame decodes one image frame; there is no timed animated GIF/video playback pipeline.
implementation: Prototype a local-only media owner in a contained process using a Windows media pipeline, with bounded files and no browser/URL support.
Mute by default, enforce resource/frame limits, obey batteryBlack and the existing timed-to-black policy, and cancel by generation.
Fall back to native black on decoder/device failure. Preserve instant hide/cancel before asynchronous cleanup.
acceptance: Malformed media, decoder hangs, device loss and rapid input cannot strand a cover or helper.
Measure CPU/GPU/memory and dismissal responsiveness against native black and scenes.
Confirm each output retains independent ownership; no burn-in effectiveness claim follows from motion.

features.title: Monitor contrast controls
features.value: Offers a small convenience for users who already want DAC to act as a broader monitor controller.
features.gap: DAC has neither contrast read/write nor generalized monitor settings.
implementation: If the brightness foundation proves reliable, add a typed contrast operation with its own advertised capability and permission.
Keep raw arbitrary VCP writes out of ordinary controls; avoid adding input-source switching to this item because it can remove the recovery display.
Reuse normalization and ownership rules where applicable and provide a manual reset path.
acceptance: Unsupported capabilities remain disabled and values are clamped to reported ranges.
Timeouts cannot block input dismissal or reuse a stale monitor handle.
Physical tests confirm recoverability without changing saved power grants.

features.title: Optional Windows screensaver bridge
features.value: Lets Windows launch DAC content for users who want an OS-managed screensaver entry.
features.gap: Hosting other savers through /p exists; DAC itself is not a registered Windows screensaver.
implementation: Treat this as a deliberate scope decision. Prototype a separate bridge handling /s, /p and /c with bounded IPC and no hardware grants.
Define who owns idle detection when Windows launches it and prevent duplicate controllers or recursion into the bridge.
Make registration and removal explicit and reversible; do not silently replace the user's existing screensaver policy.
acceptance: Fixtures cover protocol parsing, parent-window lifetime and missing controller.
An isolated visible session confirms Windows invocation, stop behavior and restoration of prior settings.
Secure Windows lock behavior is tested separately and is never inferred from a cover.

features.title: Pointer border resistance and routing
features.value: Could reduce accidental crossover into idle screens, but duplicates a specialist tool and adds input risk.
features.gap: DAC observes input; it does not redirect or constrain the cursor.
implementation: Prefer a documented coexistence recipe and compatibility tests with LittleBigMouse before considering a built-in router.
If a future fork explores routing, isolate it behind an opt-in adapter with a separate recovery shortcut and evaluate historical-event attribution.
Do not reuse current pointer position for queued events or let synthetic routing credit unrelated displays.
acceptance: Coexistence tests cover high-rate input, boundary crossing, mixed DPI and all-covered wake.
Disabling routing restores normal cursor behavior immediately.
No input interception extension proceeds without proving that the core wake invariant and recovery remain reliable.

qualification_gates.title: Physical wake and topology qualification
qualification_gates.value: Establishes whether the central per-monitor protection behavior works on real desktops.
implementation: Run the existing qualification matrix in an isolated visible Windows session across one, two and three displays, all coverage states, queued/high-rate input, hot-plug, mixed DPI, HDR and resume.
Retain executable hash, redacted timing counters, exact topology and a repeatable all-covered failure recipe. Fix defects before expanding owner/input behavior.
acceptance: Only the attributed independent target dismisses; peer generation/idle history stays intact.
Recovery is visibly reliable across repeated all-covered trials; unresolved failures remain recorded.

qualification_gates.title: Visible settings and accessibility acceptance
qualification_gates.value: Verifies that existing settings and new controls can actually be read and operated.
implementation: Check visible Edit painting, keyboard order, focus, screen-reader names, high contrast, light/dark and DPI changes.
Fix concrete failures using the current native controls before adding flyout/localization surfaces.
acceptance: Setup and recovery can be completed by keyboard and screen reader.
No hidden snapshot is counted as visible UI acceptance.

qualification_gates.title: Monitor and adapter hardware qualification
qualification_gates.value: Establishes the narrow hardware combinations on which power and later brightness features are recoverable.
implementation: Use separately authorized, operator-present tests for exact monitor/cable/dock/GPU combinations with physical recovery.
Record off, cancel, wake, timeout and quarantine behavior; preserve uncertain recovery tickets and never widen an unsupported target.
acceptance: Publish a qualified/unsupported/unknown matrix per operation and connection.
A successful simulated cycle is never substituted for physical wake evidence.

qualification_gates.title: Clean CI and trusted release preparation
qualification_gates.value: Makes delivered artifacts reproducible and reviewable outside the developer machine.
implementation: Add clean Windows CI using pinned toolchain/Fujin inputs and the existing Release/Debug, static-analysis, PE and ZIP checks.

Keep runtime tests on private desktops without startup registration or DDC. Design signing and immutable release artifacts separately; verify a final signed artifact as well as unsigned reproducibility.
acceptance: Clean CI reproduces the existing suites and retains exact source/tool identities.
Release version, resource version, archive root, manifest, signature and checksums agree.

qualification_gates.title: Real activity and endurance qualification
qualification_gates.value: Validates that common real applications and long sessions do not cause false suppression, missed wake or leaks.
implementation: Exercise browsers/native media, mute, multiple endpoints, fullscreen games, actual controllers and AC/DC transitions, then run hours/days of desktop use.
Measure resource growth and dismissal responsiveness; retain content/codec failure results. Isolate decoder work before expanding untrusted media inputs.
acceptance: Ambiguous media does not acquire unwarranted exact-tab attribution.
No sustained resource growth or stranded owned processes appears in representative runs; failures include reproducible evidence.

roadmap_decisions.reason: User marked the full command interface as a no for now; exclude it from current feature recommendations.
